newsitem.title: UK: Med crude buyers delay as Iraq heads over horizon.
newsitem.headline: Med crude buyers delay as Iraq heads over horizon.

text.p: Mediterranean crude traders said uncertainty over Iraqi exports deterred physical market discussion on Wednesday and most focussed on Algerian and Syrian term contract negotiations.
Some traders said they were still struggling to make sense of values agreed for two late July loading Russian Urals cargoes moved on Tuesday for Dated Brent -85 cents and -79/80 cents.
They said -85 cents appeared too low to reflect fair value, even allowing for the bearish influence exerted by the probable resumption of Iraq exports in late July or early August.
One trader said some sellers were asking a discount in the mid-70s for early August Urals and this was nearer the level of market talk.
"Our feeling was 85 doesn't represent the whole market. It's higher than that," another trader said.

Although four or five July Urals cargoes remain unsold, continuing uncertainty over the pricing and timing of the Iraqi sales mean most traders want to delay decisions on both the spot and term markets.
"Most people want to play for time," a trader said.

Iraq was the source of more potential bearishness on outright values on Wednesday with word from Western diplomats in New York that Bagdhad could carry over only five percent of its $1 billion quarterly limit for oil sales under the U.N. "oil-for-food" programme.

The requirement would mean Iraq would have to sell oil at a much higher rate in August -- at around 1.,5 million barrels per day (bpd) -- than was previously reckoned, or forego some of its sales under the scheme.
But some traders doubt that Iraq has the ability to produce and export as much as 1.5 million bpd.
In term discussions, Syrian oil company Sytrol has asked Dated Brent -$3.85 for Souedie and Dated Brent -40 cents for Syrian Light for August volumes.
Lifters are preparing to bid about Dated -$3.85 for Souedie and want a rollover of July's discount of 55 cents.
Customers of Algeria's Saharan Blend said they were planning to respond with bids somewhere in the 40s over Dated Brent to an offer of between 50 to 55 cents for August volumes.
They said representatives of Algerian oil company Sonatrach had told them one lifter had already agreed a premium of 53 cents but gave no details of this.
Lifters added that word of the alleged agreement would not influence their view. Saharan lifters agreed a premium of 39 to 40 cents for July material.
